title: Book One · Chapter 77: A Different Table
story:
Leo moves his chair to another table on Monday.

Ronan thinks, “Leo needs more paper.” Then Leo puts his pencil tin beside two other boys.

“Miss Wu said we can change groups for this week,” he says.

“I know.”

“I want to try their long boat.”

“Our long boat is not made yet.”

“Ours is not ready. I can try theirs now.”

Ronan looks down at the dry sheet on his desk. He kept it flat all weekend under a book. Now there are only two chairs at their table.

Mei arrives with a drawing of a flat boat. She put the small stones along the middle.

“Where is Leo?”

Ronan points.

“All right,” she says. “I want to try this.”

“You do not mind?”

“He can sit somewhere else.”

“I know that.”

She hears his tone. She holds her book still.

“Do you want to work alone today?”

“No.”

“Then help me hold this corner.”

He does. Leo is at the other table now. The boys there laugh. “This long boat will be the fastest,” someone says.

Ronan presses the paper too hard. A corner tears.

Mei pulls her hand back.

“That is the second sheet.”

He wants to blame the noise. He looks at the tear.

“I did it.”

“Yes.”

They take the sheet to Miss Wu. She is helping a child read the test card. She asks them to wait until she finishes that sentence.

Ronan stands beside the desk. Ronan looks down at the torn paper. He wants help now, but Miss Wu is busy. He holds it still while they wait.

Miss Wu gives them one narrow strip of paper, not a whole new sheet.

“Can this help the corner?”

Mei tries it. They fold the strip over the torn part. It makes that corner thicker than the others. Their boat will be different from her drawing.

They test it with one stone. It leans towards the thick corner. Ronan draws a small arrow on their page.

At the other table, Leo's boat bends in the middle. “Who pressed it?” the boys ask each other. They start to argue.

For a moment Ronan is pleased. Then Leo looks across and sees him smile.

Ronan stops smiling, but Leo saw it.

After the lesson, Leo asks, “Were you laughing at ours?”

“A little.”

“Ours was very bent.”

“Yes.”

Leo puts his tin back in his bag. “I still want to try it.”

Ronan nods. “Ours leans.”

“Like this?” Leo walks across the room with one shoulder low.

Mei puts a hand on his higher shoulder. She turns him towards the door.

“Walk properly. You will hit someone's boat.”

Mei asks Ronan to draw their next boat. She will check the fold. He hesitates. She usually makes the pictures.

“Draw our next boat,” she says. “I can add the small bits.”

He draws a long box shape with a thick corner. It is a plain picture, but she can use it. He puts his name under it. At the other table, Leo writes his group's results. He has a different job today too.

They go outside together. Leo sits at the other table again the next day. At break, he and Ronan share a game with a flat stone. Leo works with a different group. He still plays with Ronan at break. Ronan needs time to get used to this.
studyGuide:
## 重点表达

- change groups＝换组
- tears＝裂开
- leans＝倾斜
- get used to＝习惯

额外情节词（不要求本章全部记住）：strip＝纸条；thicker＝更厚；fold＝折痕。

## 读句提示

**The boys there laugh.**

那里的男孩们／笑。把“某人说……将……”改成孩子自己直接说的话。

## 理解问题

1. Leo换组为什么使Ronan不舒服？
2. 他们怎样继续保持朋友关系？
